# `fluxsim plan`

Execute the whole pipeline once, in memory, and write down what it saw: inputDigest, the seed-tree paths it materialised, the per-emit seam digests, and each declared fidelity block as it compiled, every epsilon included. Writes plan.json and seed-paths.ndjson under the run directory, and stages the rows it generated there too, so that apply --run-id commits them instead of generating them again. A child table that a counts entry lays out comes out grouped by parent in row order, as a table loaded parent by parent does; a consumer that needs another order sorts it. The child's own key is laid out from the row index, so a number or date key in ascending order gives a parent's children consecutive keys, and a text or UUID key, permuted, does not.

## Synopsis

```text
fluxsim plan [options] <bundle>
```

## Examples

```bash
# record what a run would do
fluxsim plan ./bundle

# keep the run state somewhere else
fluxsim plan ./bundle --state-dir ./.flux

# plan the run under kernel 0.1.0
fluxsim plan ./bundle --kernel 0.1.0

# record the plan only, without staging rows
fluxsim plan ./bundle --no-stage

# plan ten times the rows, and time it
fluxsim plan ./bundle --scale 10 --timings
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `bundle` | path to the FLUX bundle directory |

## Options

| Option | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--simulation-id` | `SIMULATION_ID` | which Simulation document to resolve (default: the bundle's only one) |
| `--zone` | `ZONE` | declared run zone, for sovereignty checks |
| `--kernel` | `VERSION` | the kernel the new plan takes, one of 0.1.0, 0.2.0 (default 0.2.0). The plan records it, and apply, replay, verify and ship run the kernel their plan names; 0.2.0's streams are counter-based and its continuous draws binary64 (docs/spec/KERNEL-SPEC-2.md), so its digests differ from 0.1.0's |
| `--no-stage` |  | write only plan.json and the seed paths; apply --run-id then generates the rows itself, as a plan did before it staged them (refused for a bundle that declares generator plugins, whose bytes are stored and never generated again) |
| `--allow-generator` | `NAME` | allow the generator plugin of that entry-point name to be imported and run, when the plan generates the rows; repeat it for each plugin the bundle declares under generators (without it the command is refused, FLX-3119, before anything is imported); a plugin is trusted code that runs with your rights, so name only plugins you have reviewed; no environment variable and no bundle key allows one |
| `--scale` | `F` | multiply every emit's rows, the records bounds of its fidelity block and the span of every integer or decimal key column that declares a range, by F (above 0, at most 1000000); the plan records it and apply reads it back, and 1 changes nothing; a table built from the run's events is left as it is |
| `--timings` |  | print where the time went (load, compile, each emit, framing, attestation); the numbers are wall-clock seconds, reported and recorded nowhere in a run's files |
| `--jobs` | `N` | the most processes that may generate the rows of an emit declared by statistics: a number (never more than one per CPU) or auto for one per CPU; the run summary says how many it used, and the rows and every digest are the same whatever the number (default: FLUX_JOBS, else 1) |
| `--strict-coverage` |  | refuse the run when a column falls back to a type default (an optional column nothing maps onto, a DATE or TIMESTAMP column with no declaration of its own), with a table of every such column (FLX-3304), or when the contract declares what the run does not generate, such as a check without generates or, on kernel 0.1.0 or in a Simulation that does not declare copies: true, sharedColumns or sharedAttribute (FLX-3305), before any row is drawn; a Simulation can ask for the same with strictCoverage: true in its extensions; without either the plan names those columns and goes on, and with this flag the rows and every digest are the same either way |
| `--profile` | `PATH` | the profile document the Simulation pins under extensions['com.agentics.flux/1'].profile (docs/spec/PROFILE-SPEC.md); refused when its digest is not the pinned one, and when the Simulation pins none |
| `--state-dir` | `STATE_DIR` | run-state directory (default: ./.flux) |
| `-j, --json` |  | emit machine-readable JSON |
